- [2023/05/25] The appellant argued that they were not responsible for the installation of flashing around windows due to specific contractual terms.
- [2023/05/25] The respondents claimed that the contract terms were superseded by a Deed, specifically clause 14, which constituted the entire agreement.
- [2023/05/25] The appellant referenced clause 7 of the Deed, arguing it preserved the original contract terms.
- [2023/05/25] The Tribunal preferred the expert evidence of Mr. Brennan over Mr. Sim regarding the necessity of flashing for windows.
- [2023/05/25] Mr. Brennan's report from May 17, 2020, stated that flashing was necessary to prevent moisture egress between the window frame and the house frame.
- [2023/05/25] Mr. Sim argued that additional flashing was unnecessary due to the use of commercial-grade sections and sub-heads/sills.
- [2023/05/25] The Tribunal concluded that the windows were defective due to the absence of small joint sealant, not just the absence of flashing.
- [2023/05/25] The Tribunal rejected the appellant's submission that the builder was responsible for flashing, determining the windows required replacement due to defects.
- [2023/05/25] The Tribunal found that the absence of flashing contributed to leakage but did not alter the conclusion of window defects.
- [2023/05/25] The Tribunal concluded that clause 14 of the Deed did not exclude reference to the original contract terms regarding the appellant's obligations.
